questions.question: You developed a JavaFX Store Management System using MVC and MySQL. Can you describe its architecture, how responsibilities were separated across the model, view, and controller layers, and a design decision you would change for a cloud-based production system?
In your payments work on World Link, ACH, and EDI, how did you translate business requirements into test scenarios and ensure coverage of high-risk payment flows?

Describe a database-testing issue you identified using MySQL, Oracle SQL Developer, or SQL/PLSQL. How did you investigate the data, determine the root cause, and communicate it to developers and business stakeholders?
This role involves Java 11 or 17. What Java features, coding practices, and testing approaches would you apply when building a maintainable backend service in a modern Java version?

How would you design the data model for a payment-processing microservice that must track payment status, beneficiaries, currencies, audit history, and failures? Which parts would you use a relational database for versus a NoSQL database?

Suppose a Java payment service must be containerized and deployed on AWS with Docker and Kubernetes. What would you include in the Docker image, Kubernetes deployment configuration, and operational monitoring setup?

You have experience coordinating walkthroughs, defect calls, and training sessions with clients, management, developers, and test teams. Describe a situation where stakeholders had different interpretations of a requirement and how you helped drive resolution.
What approach would you take to define integration, regression, and performance test coverage for a set of microservices that communicate asynchronously and process financial transactions?

You trained new hires and helped colleagues resolve questions on testing concepts and banking-domain workflows. How would you mentor a junior engineer who is implementing a Java service but is struggling with debugging, test design, or understanding the domain?

The role values Git and GitOps practices. How would you structure source-control workflows and deployment promotion processes for a Java service so that changes are reviewable, traceable, and safely released across environments?
